ext.minecraft_startup_editor.core.hint: Always included. Required for container compatibility.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.core.zgcHin: ParallelRefProcEnabled is hidden — not applicable under ZGC.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.gc.none.des: Run with JVM defaults — no explicit GC flags applied.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.memory.limi: This server is allocated {memory} MB, so the heap is capped at {budget} MB.
The initial heap size the JVM allocates at startup. Lower values reduce startup memory; higher values reduce GC pressure early on. Recommended: 25% of allocated server RAM.
The maximum heap size the JVM may use. It is capped below the container memory limit so the JVM has room for metaspace, thread stacks and direct buffers — a heap sized to the whole allocation starts and then dies under load. Recommended: 85% of allocated server RAM.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.aika: Best for: Java 8–20 servers. Classic G1GC tuning by Aikar. For Java 21+, ZGC is now the recommended choice.

A well-known set of G1GC JVM flags originally published by Aikar. Reduces GC pause times and avoids common Minecraft-related GC issues. Recommended for Java 8–20 servers. For Java 21+, consider ZGC for lower pause times. Best results on 4–16 GB RAM.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.alwa: Best for: stable tick pacing on all servers. Tradeoff: slower startup due to full heap pre-allocation.
-XX:+AlwaysPreTouch forces the JVM to allocate and touch all heap memory at startup. This prevents lazy allocation from causing lag spikes during gameplay when new memory regions are first accessed.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.disa: Best for: avoiding plugin-triggered pause spikes. Tradeoff: explicit GC calls from plugins are ignored.

-XX:+DisableExplicitGC prevents code from triggering explicit garbage collection via System.gc(). Some poorly-written plugins call this, causing unexpected GC pauses. Disabling it lets the JVM manage GC automatically.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.g1gc: Best for: conservative baselines, compatibility checks, or debugging. Tradeoff: less tuned than Aikar's G1GC.
Enables the G1 garbage collector with JVM defaults. Use this only if you want a simple baseline or if Aikar's flags cause issues. Not compatible with ZGC, Shenandoah, or Aikar's flags.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.jit_: Best for: all server types. Benefit: better long-run CPU efficiency as hot paths are optimized.
Turns on -XX:+TieredCompilation (multi-tier JIT) and -XX:+OptimizeStringConcat. Generally beneficial for all Minecraft servers; helps reduce CPU usage over time as hot code paths are compiled.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.log4: Best for: all server types. Benefit: defense-in-depth against Log4Shell-style lookup abuse.

Adds -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true to block the Log4Shell exploit. Modern Minecraft versions (1.18.1+) ship a patched log4j, but this flag is harmless and provides defence-in-depth for all versions.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.nati: Best for: Java 21+ servers. Benefit: suppresses JNA restricted method warnings that will become errors in a future Java release.

--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED allows JNA (Java Native Access) to call restricted native methods without warnings. In Java 21+ these generate warnings; in a future release they will become errors. Recommended for Java 21+; automatically forced on for Java 25+.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.pape: Best for: Paper-family servers on Java 16+. Benefit: avoids module-access errors and reflective warnings.

Paper and its forks (Purpur, Folia) need access to internal JDK classes via the Java module system. These --add-opens flags are required on Java 16+ and prevent reflective-access warnings and crashes. Only relevant for Paper-based servers.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.para: Best for: object-heavy workloads. Benefit: faster reference processing during GC and lower pause pressure.

-XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled allows the garbage collector to process soft, weak, and phantom references in parallel during GC. This can significantly reduce GC pause times on servers with many objects.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.shen: Best for: low-pause setups on Java 11+ when ZGC is unavailable. Tradeoff: tuning ecosystem is less common than G1GC.

ShenandoahGC performs concurrent compaction to keep pause times very low. Available from Java 11 and uses the incremental-update (iu) mode for broadest compatibility. Good alternative when ZGC is not available. Not compatible with G1GC or ZGC options.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.stri: Best for: memory-constrained G1GC servers with many duplicate strings. Tradeoff: small additional GC CPU work.

Enables -XX:+UseStringDeduplication, which causes G1GC to merge identical String objects in the heap. Reduces memory usage on servers with many duplicate strings (chat, items). Requires G1GC; not compatible with ZGC or Shenandoah.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.term: Best for: container or headless consoles. Benefit: more reliable terminal behavior and readable color output.

Sets -Dterminal.jline=false -Dterminal.ansi=true. Helps avoid terminal issues in containerized or headless environments and keeps colour output readable. Commonly useful for modded server consoles, but safe for all server types.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.option.use_: Best for: containerized hosting (Docker/M12labs). Benefit: JVM respects cgroup memory limits correctly.

-XX:+UseContainerSupport makes the JVM container-aware so it correctly reads memory limits from Docker/M12labs. Without this, the JVM may see the host machine's total RAM instead of the container limit.
Best for: Java 21+ servers. Mojang's default as of Minecraft 26.1. Lowest pause times. Tradeoff: slightly higher memory overhead.

ZGC with the Generational extension (Java 21+) provides sub-millisecond GC pauses. Recommended for Java 21+ servers. For Java 25+, automatically uses Compact Object Headers and String Deduplication (Mojang's defaults for Minecraft 26.1). Not compatible with G1GC-based options.

ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.basi: The recommended set of flags for every Minecraft server: Aikar's G1GC, JIT compiler optimisations, terminal-compatibility fixes, and Log4Shell mitigation.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.larg: Combines Aikar's G1GC flags with JIT compiler optimisations, Log4Shell mitigation, and terminal compatibility fixes. Best suited to large modded environments where startup footprint and classpath size are higher than average.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.low_: Uses Java 21's Generational ZGC (-XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational) for the lowest possible GC latency. Best for servers with 16 GB+ of dedicated RAM and Java 21.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.pape: Enables Aikar's G1GC flags, String Deduplication for memory savings, JIT optimisations, Paper module-system opens, and Log4Shell mitigation. Ideal for high-player-count Paper or Purpur servers.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.secu: Aikar's G1GC combined with the Log4Shell mitigation flag and terminal-compat fixes. The security flag is harmless on patched versions but adds defence-in-depth for older modpacks running legacy Minecraft.
ext.minecraft_startup_editor.preset.vani: A clean, minimal flag set: basic G1GC, JIT optimisations, and Log4Shell mitigation. Use this when you want a simple baseline without aggressive tuning.
